findings.title: Customers keep queueing at a till the player picked up in build mode, and follow it around the store
findings.detail: `BuildMode.pick()` has no customer check. `sell_refusal` refuses with "Someone is at this till" (build_mode.gd:241-244), but nothing stops you moving a checkout while people are queued or being served. Build mode can also be opened while the store is OPEN (`enter()` only checks your hands and tool). Once the till is carried, `_checkout_ok()` only checks that it is valid, in the tree and not queued for deletion. It never calls `world.in_use(checkout)`, unlike `_slot_has` at :232. So `_queue_tick` keeps running and `_queue_walk` calls `queue_spot_for()` every tick from the ghost's live `global_transform`. Queued customers walk after the floating till. `Checkout._physics_process` can also `begin()` the front customer and unload items onto the moving counter. Fix: in `pick()`, refuse a `Checkout` with `customer`, a non-empty `queue` or a cashier, the same way `sell_refusal` does. Also add `and shopper.world.in_use(checkout)` to `_checkout_ok()`, so a carried till sends its queue to `_join_queue()`.
findings.note: customer_test regression (till with queue can't be picked up; carried till's queue moves)

findings.title: The front customer at an unstaffed till never moves to a till that is being served
findings.detail: `Checkout._physics_process` calls `begin(queue[0])` as soon as the front customer is `ready_at_till()`, whether or not anyone is serving; it only rings the bell. `begin()` sets them to AT_TILL. The AT_TILL branch of `_queue_tick` never calls `_maybe_switch_queue()`, which only runs in QUEUE. A common case: you serve at till 1, a cashier works till 2, and you leave to restock. The C5 fix moves everyone behind the front customer to till 2. The front customer stands at till 1 with their basket on the counter for the full 90 s of `patience_s`, then drops the basket and leaves. That is lost sales, a mess and about −15 satisfaction, while the cashier at till 2 has nobody to serve. Fix: in the IDLE branch, only `begin()` when `is_attended()` or no attended till with room exists. Otherwise leave them in QUEUE so the 2.5 s switch check can move them.
findings.note: checkout_test regression fails before, passes after

findings.title: Each list entry buys one unit, and repeated entries for the same product stack penalties and contradict each other
findings.detail: This confirms the lead. `pick_list` draws with replacement, so the same product can appear on a list several times. Each entry is a separate trip, price roll and `remove_one`. An unstocked product listed twice costs −12 twice (−24) and two lost sales; the second bark is dropped because they are still talking. At +40% the customer can say "I'm not paying $X for that" and grab the same item 0.3 s later (refuse chance 16% per roll). Nobody buys a six-pack's worth, as Supermarket Simulator customers do. Fix: turn the list into `{id: qty}` and merge duplicates. Draw the quantity from a new `customers.json` `quantity` table, optionally per product. Make one price decision and one OOS or refuse penalty per product. Take `min(qty, stock)` units across slots and show all of them in the basket.

findings.title: Customers buy items they physically cannot reach
findings.detail: `_stand_point` snaps the spot 0.6 m in front of the slot to `nav.closest()`, which can be metres away when that spot is blocked. `BuildRules.refusal` has no rule keeping slot fronts clear, so two shelves can be placed face to face with a gap under 0.6 m, or a shelf front against another fixture's back. TO_SLOT then calls `_reach_in()` whenever `follow()` returns true or they stop walking, with no distance check. The customer takes stock from the end of the aisle, through a shelf. `_nearest_slot` also ranks slots by straight-line distance through fixtures, so it prefers such a blocked slot. Fix: in `_stand_point`, if the snapped point is more than about 0.3 m from the intended one, treat the slot as unreachable and try the next nearest. Check that the customer is within 0.5 m of the stand point before `_reach_in`. Add a front-clearance rule (about 0.7 m) to `BuildRules.refusal`.
findings.note: Build-rule half of N4 (front clearance) also landed

findings.title: No crowd avoidance: customers pass through each other and walk through the player, who cannot get past them
findings.detail: This confirms the lead. `collision_mask = Mk.LAYER_WORLD` for shoppers, and staff and Dale do the same. The ARCHITECTURE doc says this is deliberate ("people pass through each other"). Everyone walks to the exact same `DOOR_IN` point, the exact same stand point for a slot, and one of two spawn points. The spawner's `while pending` loop (customer_spawner.gd:41-43) can spawn several customers in one frame at the same `EXITS` point, so they walk the same path inside each other. The player's mask includes `LAYER_NPCS`, so it is one-sided. Customers walk into your capsule, and the physics probably pushes you out when you next move [INFERENCE: Jolt depenetration]. Meanwhile someone picking an item, or an overflow queuer told to "wait where they are" for up to 90 s, blocks your way down a 1 m aisle completely. Fix: add `LAYER_NPCS | LAYER_PLAYER` to the walker mask. Use navmesh avoidance (`NavigationServer3D` agents with `velocity_computed`) or a cheap separation steer. Spread out stand points and `DOOR_IN` per customer, and space out spawns.
findings.note: nav_test: head-on walkers keep >0.35 m and still arrive; windowed tour ran clean

findings.title: Trolleys go through shelves at every pick and every corner
findings.detail: The trolley sits at `TROLLEY_OFFSET` (0, 0, −0.78), in front of the body. The checkout code says it sticks out about 0.9 m. The stand point is only `REACH_STAND` = 0.6 m from the slot front, and `_reach_in` turns the body to face the shelf. The trolley's origin ends up about 0.18 m inside the fixture, with most of its length inside. Paths are planned for a 0.3 m agent radius, so the trolley also cuts through shelf ends at every turn. R2's C8 fixed this only at the till. Fix: trolley users stop beside the shelf. Leave the trolley at the stand point lined up with the aisle (`top_level`), and face the shelf from beside it. Or add the trolley length to the stand distance and to a larger nav radius for trolley customers.

findings.title: Customers know an item is out of stock without looking, and complain wherever they happen to be
findings.detail: `_find_slot_or_lose` checks every slot in the store instantly. With none in stock, the "No {product}? Seriously?" bark and the −12 happen where the customer is standing, often by the door or at the previous shelf. They never walk to the empty shelf, which still has its label (`remove_one(true)` keeps `product_id`). You cannot tell which shelf is the problem. Supermarket Simulator customers go to the spot and react there. Fix: if a labelled slot with count 0 exists for the product, walk to it, play a short look-around, then complain. Fall back to complaining in place only when no slot is labelled for it.

findings.title: Customers keep staring back at the shelf for 2.5 s after a bark at the shelf
findings.detail: `tick` only resets `look_weight` while `not bark.is_talking()`. At the shelf the weight is 1 with `look_target` on the slot front. A forced refusal bark or a `great_prices` bark then moves the state to BROWSE. The weight stays at 1 for the 2.5 s bark, and the target is not updated unless you are within 4 m. The customer walks to the next item with their head turned up to 70° back at the old shelf. When you are nearby, they stare at where you stood when they started talking. Fix: drop `look_weight` to 0 when leaving PICK unless they are talking to you. While talking within 4 m, update `look_target` to the player camera every tick.

findings.title: The arrival cap counts customers walking along the footpath and through the car park
findings.detail: `live_count()` counts everyone in the `shoppers` group. Customers start and end at `EXITS` (−22.5, 29.5) and (16.5, 29.5), about 38 m and 35 m in a straight line from `DOOR_IN`. At 1.2–1.6 m/s that is roughly 22–32 s each way, about 45–60 s of every visit spent outside, all counted against `2 + 4·tills + level/2`. With 6 slots on day 1, a large share are on the pavement while the store sits empty. The spawner, `Game` CLOSING and the open sign also wait for that walk. Fix: leave customers in LEAVE who are past the door out of the cap, keeping the hard 20 for performance. Or start and end them at the parked-car bays (`ParkedCars`), much closer to the door.

findings.title: Fair, well-run service cannot earn more than about 3.85 stars
findings.detail: Satisfaction starts at 70, which is already 3.5 stars, and the only positive events are bargain (+3, only at ≤85% of market), promo (+2 once) and fast service (+5). A fully stocked, fairly priced visit with quick service ends at 70 + 5 + 2 = 77, or 3.85 stars. Any single out-of-stock (−12) drops it below 3.5. `fast_service_s` = 20 s counts from joining the queue, including the walk to the lane and 0.35 s per item to unload (`UNLOAD_STEP`), so trolley customers rarely get it. The M9 soak sits at 3.04 stars on day 30. Good play is not rewarded unless you sell below market. Fix: add positive events in `customers.json`, such as found every item (+8), a fair price at or under market (+1 per item), and a clean store (+3). Or lower `start` and rebalance.

findings.title: Basket and bag follow the hands one frame late from physics

On displays faster than 60 Hz the basket probably trails or jitters against the hand [UNVERIFIED: needs a windowed run]. Fix: put `BoneAttachment3D` nodes on RightHand and LeftHand in `HumanRig.setup` and parent the carrier and bag to them with fixed offsets.

findings.title: Paying bills with negative cash makes every bill bigger
findings.detail: `complete_sale` adds `sale.net()` to `money` without a floor. `net()` is `charged - over_changed`, and the change tray has no limit (`checkout.gd:681-684` appends any note). So handing over a $100 note by mistake when cash is low, which is common on day 1 after spending the $600 on stock, leaves `money` below zero. In `pay_bills`, `part := mini(money, cents)` is then negative. `b["paid"] = part` stores that negative number, and `unpaid = cents - part` becomes `cents + |money|`. Each of tonight's bills goes overdue at its full amount plus the whole cash deficit, plus 10% on top. With four bills, the deficit is counted four times. The receipt sees `paid < 0`, so it shows no PAID or UNPAID tag. Fix: `var part := clampi(money, 0, int(b["cents"]))` in both loops, and the same in `pay_overdue`.

findings.title: The third short night ends the game with no warning, no way out, and wrong advice on screen

The receipt tells the player "Pay them at the Bank on the PC", so they clear everything. The Bank then hides the streak, because `_fill_overdue` returns "Nothing overdue." before it draws the warning. If they end that night even 1¢ short, repossession is certain. Holding E on the sign gives no warning. On the receipt the only button is "Pay all", and `loan_refusal` returns "The bank is closed" in SUMMARY, so they can't borrow to cover it. The run is lost with no chance to react; only the clipboard's red total hints at it. Fix: show the streak in the Bank and the HUD whenever it is above 0. When streak + 1 would reach `repossession_days` and cash is below `bills_due()`, block or confirm End day at the sign. Allow loans in SUMMARY before Pay all. Change the receipt text to "Clear them and cover tonight's bills, or the bank takes the store on night N".

findings.title: Customer numbers don't grow with store size, so expansions E4–E8 and tills 5–6 only add cost
findings.detail: The in-store cap is `min(20, 2 + 4·tills + L/2)`. Floor area plays no part, and the cap is already 20 with 4 tills from L4, or 3 tills from L12. Arrivals above the cap wait in `pending` and are thrown away at 22:00 (`customer_spawner.gd:28-31`). Buying E4–E8 adds $25–40 a day in rent plus $1.50 a cell in electricity for no extra customers; E8 alone is $7,500. Tills 5–6, sold up to `max: 6`, can't raise the cap. The M9 soak in PROGRESS.md shows customers flat at about 101–117 a day from day 14 to day 30. The AI held $3k–6k cash on days 21–24 and still didn't expand, and it never bought E6–E8. The end of the build-out is a trap. Fix: make the cap depend on unlocked floor area or cells, e.g. `base + per_till·tills + per_cell·cells`, with a higher hard cap. Also correct the stale comment and defaults at customer_rules.gd:34-37, which still say `4 + 2·tills`.

Taking any of them leads straight to overdue bills and, under E2, repossession, unless what you buy pays back the full instalment from the first day. PROGRESS M9 confirms the soak AI had to be stopped from borrowing except for tills and licences. In practice the choice is "never borrow". findings.title: Fair prices top out around 3.85 stars, and stars fall as you level up
findings.detail: Satisfaction starts at 70 (3.5★). The only gains are +3 per item sold at ≤0.85× market (a loss-leader), +2 once near a promo stand, and +5 for fast service. A perfect visit at market price or above therefore peaks at 77, about 3.85★. 4.5★ needs about five loss-leader items per customer, so the newspaper's "worth crossing town" headline can't be reached without selling below market. Lists grow with level (`1 + randi()%(2+L)`), and each item adds another −12 out-of-stock chance, so stars sink as you progress: the soak shows 3.6 at L5 against 2.2–3.0 at L8–16. Stars only scale arrivals by `0.4 + 0.12·stars`, and once E3's cap binds they don't matter at all. Fix: add positive events (item found, clean store, short queue, a well-stocked basket), or score satisfaction relative to the list size.

findings.title: Progression runs out around day 27, and two of the 16 levels unlock only a colour
findings.detail: Max level is 16, which the soak reaches on day 27. Nothing exists after it: no prestige, no new licences, no reason to keep earning, and E3 makes the late expansions worthless anyway. L13 unlocks only a sky blue uniform and L16, the final level, only a hot pink trim. L7 is just S2 and L11 just S3. findings.title: The day-length option changes income while bills stay the same
findings.detail: Arrivals are counted per in-game hour (`delta * clock.rate()`), but walking, shopping and checkout take real seconds, and the cap counts shoppers alive in real time. Once the cap binds, customers per day are roughly cap × real day length ÷ visit time. An 8-minute day serves about a third fewer customers than a 12-minute one [INFERENCE: 20 × 480 s / ~150 s ≈ 64 against ≈ 96]. A 20-minute day serves more, yet rent, wages and loans are charged per day. Picking "short days" in Options quietly cuts income and pushes the player toward overdue bills. Fix: scale the cap or arrival rate by `12 / day_length_min`, or tune and soak at each option.

findings.detail: In PREP the sign's hold time is 0, so the E press opens the store at once through `_try_instant_interact` (`Game.open_store`). On the same held press, `_update_hold_interact` reads the hold time again. The phase is now OPEN, so it reads 0.6 s, and `_hold_lock` is still false, so the hold keeps counting. After 0.6 s it calls `interact`, which runs `Game.close_early()`. That means a press of about 0.7 s flips the sign twice and throws away the whole trading day, with no confirm and no undo. The tutorial teaches "hold E on the sign to end the day", so players will hold E here. Fix: set `_hold_lock = true` after any instant interact (and after `try_catch`), so a hold needs a fresh press. findings.title: Selling a till moves every cashier, takes the till from the wrong one, and drops sales in progress
findings.detail: Cashier tills are indexes into `world.checkouts()`, which is just the order of the fixtures' children. `fit_tills` only resets cashiers whose index is now too high. Example: tills A, B, C with cashiers X, Y, Z; sell A. X (index 0) now works B, Y works C, and Z gets −1 and has no till. In `CashierJob.tick`, `_resolve()` returns a new checkout, so it calls `_leave_post()` (cashier = null, `_serving` = null) on B and C mid-scan or mid-payment and walks to the other till. GDD §10 says "its cashier moves to a free till or has none". Players see staff swap tills, customers left half-served, and the wrong worker standing idle on full pay. The HUD till numbers change too. Fix: key assignments to a stable till id kept on the Checkout (for example a saved `till_no`), not to the child index. In `fit_tills`, unassign only the cashier whose till went.

findings.title: Crouching and dropping a box while looking down puts it at your feet, sunk into the floor
findings.detail: The carried box sits at `CARRY_POS` in camera space. With the crouched eye at 1.0 m and pitch ≤ about −15°, the box origin works out to below y = 0 (about −0.17 m at −45°). The held box already clips through the floor. In `_free_drop_point`, all 9 probes use the same `held.y`, so each padded query overlaps the Floor (LAYER_WORLD). The function then returns `from`, the player's own x/z at that depth, without testing it. The box therefore appears inside your capsule and part-way into the floor. Crouching to stock bottom shelves and then dropping the box is a common move. [UNVERIFIED: the exact physics after the 0.4 s collision exception ends.] Fix: clamp the probe height to `maxf(held.y, global_position.y + 0.02)`, keep a minimum forward offset of about 0.5 m, and never return a point inside the player's capsule. Optionally raise CARRY_POS while crouching so the held box doesn't clip.

findings.title: Stocking two coolers side by side leaves the first door open; R takes stock through a closed door

Customers only close doors they opened themselves. `take_back_one` never calls `open_door`, so items come out through shut glass; S14 fixed the same problem for restockers. Also, `_update_box` returns on `locked` before `_close_idle_door`, so sitting at the PC or till straight after stocking leaves the door open. Fix: before switching to a new fixture, close the old `_door_fx`. Call `slot.fixture.open_door(...)` and set `_door_fx` in `take_back_one`. Run `_close_idle_door` before the `locked` return.

findings.title: Each Options slider tick rewrites settings.cfg and re-applies graphics; at the PC it undoes the full-res view
findings.detail: Every `value_changed` calls `_store`, which does a ConfigFile load and save to disk and then `changed.emit()`. `Lighting.apply_quality` runs on every emit and resets `scaling_3d_scale` and FXAA, and sets the shadow atlas and environment. Dragging a volume slider therefore writes the file about 20 times. With today's focus-loss pause, you can open Options while sitting at the PC. Any change there (even volume) sets the viewport back to 0.85 with FXAA, so ShopOS smears again (M3). Standing up then restores the `_scale_before` taken before the change. Fix: save on `drag_ended` and debounce, emit a graphics-specific signal that `apply_quality` listens to, and have PcDesk re-apply its overrides or read the preset again on unfocus.

The player clicks Save, sees nothing, and gets the toast after closing the menu. findings.title: Closing the game while Sunday's newspaper is up loses the weekly review
findings.detail: The autosave runs before `newspaper.open(...)`. `pending_review` is not in `save_state()`, and `load_state()` clears it. The head-office bonus is already in `money`, but the review and its bonus line are gone after a quit or crash on the paper. Fix: save `pending_review` and re-open the paper after loading while it is not empty, or save again after the paper closes.
findings.note: game.gd half: pending_review in save_state/load_state (+ARCHITECTURE save format). Reopen-after-load and clear-on-close in main.gd handed to lead. test_an_unread_weekly_review_survives_a_save; save_test 33/0

findings.title: A corrupt newest save leaves a Continue button that does nothing
findings.detail: `latest_slot()` goes by file modified time and only checks that the file exists. `read()` returns `{}` for bad JSON. Continue still shows (with "Slot N · empty" under it), and clicking it gets `false` back from `load_slot` with no message. It never falls back to an older slot that is fine. Fix: have `latest_slot()` skip slots where `read(n)` is empty, and show a toast when `load_slot` fails.
findings.note: latest_slot skips unreadable

findings.title: Boxes in flight are saved at their mid-air position and drop wherever they were on load
findings.detail: Saving is allowed in PREP, when deliveries happen. A box already fired is a child of Loose, so `capture` saves it as a loose box at its mid-air position. `undelivered()` only lists boxes not yet fired. On load the box falls from up to about 3 m between the van and the bay, maybe onto a parked car. Fix: in `capture`, for a box with the `in_flight` meta, save the bay spot it was heading for (`bay.allocate`), or add it to `deliveries` instead of `boxes`.
findings.note: in-flight boxes saved as deliveries; save/delivery tests pass

findings.title: `Player.box_caught` is emitted but nothing in the game listens to it
findings.detail: The only connection is in tests/cases/additions_test.gd:56. The catch's effects (XP, chime, toast, tutorial notify) already happen inline in `try_catch` and `BoxCannon.caught`. AGENTS.md says not to test wiring, and this signal exists only for that test. Fix: remove the signal and have the test check `held_box` and the XP gain instead.
findings.note: additions_test passes

findings.title: Taking exact cash from the floor leaves an empty card keypad open on an idle till
findings.detail: 5329992 added the exact-cash path. If you're standing and click or E the cash, the call goes TillTarget.on_primary → use_target → open_payment(player). Because seated==null, that calls sit(player) (653), and sit() calls open_payment(player) again (888). This inner call runs drawer.open()+give_change(), which leads to _complete→_end and sets method=&"". When control returns to the outer open_payment, `method == &"cash"` is now false, so it falls into the else branch: change_panel.close(); keypad.open() (667). The player sits down after a cash sale and sees a CARD keypad for no payment. Digits they type drive reader_typed on an idle reader. The keypad keeps whatever was typed into the next card sale, because open() only clears when it's not visible. Sitting with E while exact cash is waiting also completes the sale straight away, which contradicts "waits until the player takes it". Fix: return from open_payment as soon as `phase != Phase.PAYING` after sit(); or have sit() pass auto=true and let only the explicit cash click complete the sale.
findings.note: sit() opens payment in auto mode: exact cash waits; standing cash click books the sale and leaves no keypad/change panel open. test_exact_cash_taken_standing_leaves_no_keypad_open fails on 1724812 (2 checks), passes after; checkout_test 74/0

findings.title: Customers now pick an empty unserved till over a full served one, then give up there
findings.detail: The new ranking puts `room` ahead of `attended`. A served lane is full at 6 people (LANE_MAX 4.65 m, 0.8 m each) or 2-3 trolleys. Once that happens, every new customer joins an unattended second till. That till's front customer starts (_served_elsewhere is false because the served till has a queue), rings the bell and unloads, then waits their whole 90 s patience. AT_TILL never runs _maybe_switch_queue, so they drop the basket and leave (mess, lost sales, "give_up" quote). The rest of that queue only switches when the served till's queue_length ≤ their index. Before today, everyone joined the attended till. This hits the normal mid-game setup: a second till bought for the +4 cap while the player alone works till 1. Fix: rank attended above room. Prefer attended tills with room; if none has room, join the shortest attended queue and wait as overflow. Use unattended tills only when nobody is serving anywhere.
findings.note: shortest_queue ranks attended > room > staffed > shorter queue (world.gd swept into 84de3a0; its regression test swept into bf35689). test_a_full_served_lane_beats_an_unserved_till fails on 1724812, passes after; old full-lane test now asserts room wins only when nobody serves. checkout_test 74/0

findings.title: A Smokes customer at the unattended cigarette-wall till is held with no bell until patience runs out
findings.detail: _served_elsewhere() stops begin() whenever another in-use till is attended with an empty queue. The hold assumes _maybe_switch_queue will move the customer. A customer with counter_asks calls shortest_queue(true), which always returns the wall till, so `best == checkout` and they never switch (shopper_brain.gd:518-519). Example: the player or a cashier works till 2 with nobody queued while the wall stands behind till 1. The Smokes customer stands at till 1's serve point and nothing happens: no unload, no counter bell. Patience drains and they give up, unless someone happens to join till 2. Fix: skip the hold when queue[0].brain.counter_asks is non-empty, or when the customer can't use the served till (`w.cig_wall_till() == self`).
findings.note: _served_elsewhere now asks shortest_queue(counter_asks) like _maybe_switch_queue, so a Smokes buyer (always routed to the wall till) is never held. test_smokes_buyer_is_not_held_for_another_served_till fails on 1724812 (phase 0), passes after; m7_content 83/0

findings.title: Overflow customers freeze wherever they finished shopping, out of sight of the till
findings.detail: When `not checkout.in_lane(shopper)`, they stop() on the spot and stare at the till. That spot is usually in front of the last shelf they used, somewhere across the store, so they block other shoppers' stand points. The player can't see the real queue length, and patience burns down without any visible line. LANE_MAX (4.65 m) makes this common: 6 walkers or 2-3 trolleys fill a lane. has_room() also ignores the joiner's own trolley (_queue_depth uses null for k == size), so a trolley pusher is told there is room and then waits in place anyway. Fix: send overflow to a holding spot just past the lane end, or let the line bend along a free aisle. Count the joiner's trolley in has_room.
findings.note: overflow snakes into a 2nd column inside the kept-clear lane (in sight, out of the aisles); only past both do they wait in place; has_room/shortest_queue take the joiner's trolley. test_a_full_lane_... updated (overflow spot in lane, unique, 2nd column holds more); checkout_test 77/0, customer 54/0

findings.title: A till with a cashier can't be moved during PREP, and build mode still shows "[LMB] Move"
findings.detail: 41f4c70 made pick() refuse till_busy(fx), and till_busy includes has_cashier(). Cashiers are on shift in PREP (StaffCrew.shift_on), stand at their post and set checkout.cashier (cashier_job.gd:93). So any staffed till is locked in place exactly when players rearrange. The hover prompt still reads "[LMB] Move · …" and LMB fails with "Someone is at this till". The only way out is after hours, or reassigning or firing the cashier. Fix: ignore the cashier for pick() and have the cashier re-walk to _post() when the till lands (the queue/customer checks can stay). At minimum, say "Move it after hours or reassign the cashier".
findings.note: pick() ignores the cashier (queue/customer still block); cashier steps off while carried and returns via CashierJob._resolve; hover shows Move only when it can. test_a_staffed_till_can_be_moved_and_the_cashier_follows passes; staff_test 57/0

findings.title: The 0.6 m shelf-access strip is narrower than the navmesh can use, so "reachable" layouts still starve shelves
findings.detail: B2 now requires one face with ACCESS_DEPTH=0.6 m of free floor. The navmesh is baked with agent_radius 0.3 (world/nav.gd:91), which erodes 0.3 m from both the face and the opposite obstacle. A gap of 0.6 m to about 0.7 m therefore has no walkable cells. ShopperBrain._reachable (closest nav point within 0.6 of a stand point 0.6 out) then fails for mid-aisle slots, and customers skip them or bark "not carried". The strip check also never tests whether the strip connects to the rest of the floor. Fix: set ACCESS_DEPTH to at least REACH_STAND + agent_radius (0.9 m). Optionally confirm with a nav query once the rebake finishes.
findings.note: ACCESS_DEPTH = REACH_STAND + 0.3 = 0.9 m. Measured on the navmesh: 0.6-0.8 m aisles leave 4-8 of 12 gondola slots reachable. test_an_accepted_shelf_is_reachable_on_the_navmesh fails on old rule (x 4.75 accepted, 4/12), passes after; build_test 129/0

findings.title: Every customer walking to an empty shelf scans every slot in the store each physics frame
findings.detail: While _oos_walk is true, TO_SLOT calls _nearest_slot(_wanted) every tick. That loops all fixtures × slots (564 in a full store), calling _slot_has and in_use on each. Out-of-stock walks are frequent mid-game and last several seconds per customer. This brings back the per-frame full-slot scan that round-1 #18 removed from the spawner, while V3 (35-44 fps windowed) is still open. [UNVERIFIED cost; expect ms per frame with several walkers]. Fix: re-check on a 0.5 s timer, or listen for the product's slot count changing.
findings.note: OOS walk re-scans slots every OOS_RECHECK 0.5 s instead of every physics tick; customer_test 54/0

findings.title: Repeat Smokes picks still mean one complaint and one price decision per pack
findings.detail: c98c03f (N3) merges repeat picks into a quantity, but the counter_wall path expands them back into one counter_asks entry per unit. When the wall is empty, _ask_for_counter_items (checkout.gd:499-505) charges -12 and plays an out_of_stock bark for each pack. 3 Smokes is -36 and three bubbles. When the wall has stock, fetch_smokes (checkout.gd:578) rolls CustomerRules.decide separately for each pack, so one customer can buy a pack and then refuse the next at the same price, -8 each time. Fix: pass {id, qty} to the till. Do one has_pack check and one complaint for the shortfall, and one decide() per product with the verdict cached for the remaining packs.
findings.note: one decide() per wall product cached per customer; refusal/out-of-stock drains the remaining packs as lost sales with one complaint and one sat hit. test_several_packs_are_one_decision_and_one_complaint passes; m7_content 90/0

findings.title: Overdue paid at the Bank during the day disappears from the receipt's money lines
findings.detail: _tally_other drops reason &"overdue", which covers both tonight's overdue lines and pay_overdue (494-499) at the Bank in PREP or OPEN. A daytime Bank payment lowers cash, but it isn't in "Other money today" and isn't among tonight's overdue_before (snapshot taken after the payment). So "Cash at open + revenue + other − bills paid" no longer equals Cash, which E11 says it should. Fix: give pay_overdue its own reason (&"overdue_bank") and add "Overdue paid at the Bank" to MONEY_NAMES.
findings.note: pay_overdue spends with &overdue_bank (tallied in other money; label in lead's a16f738). bills_test asserts other_money[overdue_bank] == -paid; 22/0

findings.title: Cost basis counts free first-order boxes at full price and never removes binned stock
findings.detail: place_order books every ordered unit at cost_of(id), including the q["free_boxes"] that cost nothing, so day-1 COGS and profit show money never spent. _use_basis (611) only runs on sales. Units that leave any other way, such as a box binned with stock in it, stay in the held count and skew the average on later orders. Start stock is never booked at all. Fix: book free units at 0 (or cut the average by the free share). Decrement the basis wherever stock is destroyed (bin_held with count > 0, misfire losses).
findings.note: free first-order boxes (dearest first, as quote prices them) booked at 0; Game.write_off_stock(id, units) removes binned units (player.bin_held hook requested from lead); no start stock exists to book. test_free_boxes_cost_nothing_and_binned_stock_leaves_the_average; day_test 46/0

findings.title: The level-16 Head office franchise never pays for itself in a normal run
findings.detail: It costs $10,000 and pays $100 per star each Sunday (game.gd:1150). At 4.35 stars that is about $435 a week, so it takes about 23 weeks (over 160 days) to break even. Level 16 arrives around day 27 at about $2,000 a day (PROGRESS M9 playtest notes), so the "real unlock" is a money sink nobody should buy. Fix: pay per day (e.g. $50/star each night) or cut the price to about $2,500. Show payback days on the card.
findings.note: price $10,000 -> $6,000, Sunday pay $100 -> $1,000 per star: 12 days payback at 3.5 stars, 10 at 4.35; card text states it; ECONOMY.md table + rationale. test_late_upgrades_do_something asserts payback <= 2 weeks, 5/0

findings.title: The "found everything" +8 is still paid when the Smokes they asked for were sold out or refused
findings.detail: Only _find_slot_or_lose and _take set _let_down. _ask_for_counter_items (wall empty, checkout.gd:499-505), fetch_smokes (out of stock or too dear, 573-582) and _lose_counter_asks never set it. A customer who complained "no Smokes" therefore still gets +8 at checkout. Fix: set customer.brain._let_down = true (via a brain method) on each of those paths.
findings.note: wall misses and lost counter asks set _let_down via ShopperBrain.let_down(); asserted in the same test

findings.title: The receipt says a cashier lets in more customers, and counts close-early arrivals as "store full"
findings.detail: max_concurrent(tills, level) has no staff term, so "Another till or a cashier lets more people in at once" is wrong about cashiers. Also, CustomerSpawner books all `pending` as turned away whenever phase != OPEN (customer_spawner.gd:30), including after a voluntary close_early. Those people show as "Turned away, store full" with advice to buy a till. Fix: drop "or a cashier". Only count pending at the 22:00 close, or tag close-early leavers separately.

findings.title: Load and save create overfilled boxes stacked on one spot
findings.detail: V1's overflow spawns one box with all `spare` units. Old 3×-multiplier chest-freezer slots can leave dozens, far beyond units_per_box, and put_one then refuses because the box is "full". The box spawns 0.8 m in front of the slot, which can be inside the next fixture in a tight aisle, and before later fixtures are added and without _hold_still. Dropped-basket saving (save.gd:79-82) also puts every product's box at the same point (basket position + 0.3), and they burst apart on load. Fix: split into ceil(n / units_per_box) boxes, offset each box's spawn point, and add them to the restored list that _hold_still freezes.

findings.title: Customers bounce between tills when the player walks past a counter
findings.detail: is_attended() counts the player just standing in the 2.5 × 5.2 m box behind a counter. Walking behind till A on the way to till B makes A "attended with an empty queue". B's front customer is then held by _served_elsewhere and moves to A at the next 2.5 s check. When the player sits at B, A is unattended and the same rule sends them back. Fix: use only seated or cashier (is_staffed()) for _served_elsewhere and _maybe_switch_queue, and keep the standing-behind check for picking a queue.

findings.title: Following the tutorial gives a nearly empty, nearly unprofitable day 1
findings.detail: The tutorial (and its 4 free boxes) has the player stock 4 of the 9 starter products. Variety is 4/12 = 0.33, just above its 0.3 floor. Arrivals are (2.5+1)·(0.4+0.12·3)·0.33 ≈ 0.89 an hour × time curve, which works out to about 13 customers over the 12-minute day. The first one shows up about 1.6 real minutes after opening, plus about 25 s walking from the footpath. Revenue is about 13 × 1.85 items × $2.66 ≈ $64, and bills are rent $20 + lights $17 + cooler/till $8 = $45, so net is about +$20. That is below the $40–$120 day-1 pacing band, and the first minutes after opening have nothing happening. These numbers come from the formulas, not a playtest [INFERENCE]. Fix: make the free order 8 boxes and have the tutorial ask for 6–8 kinds (Chipz, Crunch, Cola, Fizz, Candy, Noodle, Soup, Bread), or raise `variety_min` to about 0.5 for day 1.

findings.title: The tutorial's bay arrow points at the shop door, not the delivery bay
findings.detail: The arrow aims at `w.delivery.bay.global_position`. Neither DeliveryService nor DeliveryBay is ever positioned, and the bay works in raw world coordinates through `centre = (7.5, 4.5)`. So the arrow points at (0, 1.2, 0), the shop entrance, about 8.6 m from the bay marking. screenshot_tour.gd:171 looks at the same wrong point, so its "arrow on bay" shot couldn't catch this. findings.title: The "van" step finishes unseen while the player is still at the PC, and its catch instruction can't be done
findings.detail: The van stops about 4.5 s after Order, then 0.8 s settle, 0.5 s aim and about 1.4 s of flight. The first box lands about 7 s after ordering, which fires `delivery_landed`. The player is sitting at the PC 17 m from the bay with the hint hidden. Step 2 ("Press E as a box flies past to catch it") and its arrow are almost never shown, and from the PC a catch is impossible anyway. When they stand up, step 3 says "Carry a box inside" with no arrow to where the boxes are. Fix: finish the van step when the player first comes within about 6 m of a landed box (not on the landing), keep the arrow until then, and change the text to "the van fires boxes into the bay; walk out and fetch them (press E on one still flying to catch it for XP)".

findings.title: Nothing at the PC tells you how to leave it
findings.detail: Sitting down hides the HUD, the prompt overlay and the tutorial card. ShopOS has no exit button, and its only "Close" closes the app window, leaving you on an empty desktop. Only Esc stands you up, and nothing says so. The till view shows "Esc to stand up" and the phone shows "P or Esc to put it away", but the PC (the first thing every new player uses) shows nothing. Fix: add a "Stand up (Esc)" button to the ShopOS top bar that calls `PcDesk.unfocus()`, and change the PC prompt to "[E] Use the PC  ·  Esc to stand up".

findings.title: Ordering fewer than 4 boxes throws away the rest of the free order
findings.detail: `place_order` sets `free_order_boxes = 0` as soon as any free box is used. Ordering just the Cola first makes it free and silently cancels the other 3 free boxes. Before Order nothing warns about this, and the cart lines show full price for free boxes, so they don't add up to the $0.00 total. Fix: subtract only the boxes used (`free_order_boxes -= q.free_boxes`), and show "free" on the covered cart lines.

findings.title: The tutorial goes strictly in order and shows the wrong instructions at the till
findings.detail: A step only advances when its own event fires. Skip the optional F price check and the card is stuck on "Aim at a price label and press F" while customers queue, so the serving instructions (sit with E, click items, the reader) are never shown. If the first customer pays cash, the card tells you to click the card reader, which does nothing for cash. Nothing stops the tutorial after day 1 (GDD §13 says day 1 only), so a missed step stays on screen for days. Fix: advance past "prices" once the store opens, show the cash or card step to match the current `Checkout.method` while a payment is waiting, and stop the tutorial on the day-1 `day_ended`.

findings.title: Products you never stocked are reported as "out of stock"
findings.detail: About 15% of list picks are any licensed product. When a product isn't carried, `_find_slot_or_lose` books it as `&"out_of_stock"`, the same reason as an emptied shelf. The receipt then shows "out of stock N" on a day nothing ran out, Sunday's paper says "Bread kept running out" for bread you never sold, and the critic's stars are docked for it. Fix: book `&"not_carried"` when `ran_out` is false, show it on the receipt as "not stocked (demand)", and keep it out of `oos_products` and the out-of-stock penalty.

findings.title: Starter snacks fit only 2–6 to a shelf, so a box spans 4 slots and shelves look bare
findings.detail: CHIPZ and CRUNCH are 0.30 × 0.36 × 0.12 m: two across in a 0.6 m slot needs 0.64 m, so they fit 1 across × 3 deep = 3 a slot. CANDY (a 120 g pack modelled 26 × 36 cm) fits 6, and BREAD (0.42 m long) fits 2. A box of 12, 20 or 8 takes 4 re-aims, and a 60 cm shelf with 3 bags looks empty. This is the same oversizing S3 fixed for cans, now on the products day 1 uses. Fix: real sizes with `model_scale` as for COLA (chips about 0.22 × 0.30 × 0.08, candy about 0.15 × 0.20 × 0.05, bread about 0.28 × 0.12 × 0.12), giving 8–16 a slot.
findings.note: CHIPZ/CRUNCH model_scale 0.58 (12/slot, was 3), CANDY 0.6 (15, was 6), BREAD 0.65 (6, was 2), sizes scaled to match. stock_test capacity checks (fail before); full suite 1127/1 -> m1 label count updated, passes; soak 10 4 /tmp/cts_soak_f10 day1 $70.62 day3 $191.31 day7 $515.71 all ok

findings.title: One click buys an expansion or licence, with no confirmation and no way back
findings.detail: "Buy" charges at once. E1 costs $500 at level 2 and raises rent and lights from $37 to about $76 a day for good. On day 2–3 with about $600 cash, one stray click while browsing can start an overdue spiral. Del-to-sell (B1) and Fire (Y4) were given confirmations, but these two irreversible buys were not. Fix: use the same press-again pattern ("Buy" → "Confirm $500 · rent +$39/day" for 3 s).
findings.note: Buy arms a 3 s 'Confirm $500 · rent + lights +$39/day' (expansions) / 'Confirm $250' (licences), second press buys; progression_test (one press buys nothing, label Confirm, second buys; fails before) and m5 acceptance click-through pass

findings.title: The clipboard's range warning can't be met at level 1
findings.detail: It compares the shelves with `variety_divisor` (12) and shows "Range: 9 of 12 kinds for full traffic" in the warning colour. The Starter licence only has 9 products, so a fully stocked level-1 store is warned all day with no way to act on it. Fix: compare with the products you're licensed for, e.g. "9 of 9 you can sell · a licence adds more".
findings.note: Clipboard.range_note(n, sellable): warns only when kinds you're licensed for are missing; 9 of 9 reads '9 of 9 you can sell · a licence adds more' in ink. progression_test covers 9/9, 5/9, 14/30; passes

findings.title: The tutorial card rebuilds itself every frame while you sit at the PC
findings.detail: `_process` checks `visible != (w != null and not current().is_empty())` but ignores `_hidden_for_pc`. At the PC, `visible` is false and the right side is true, so `refresh()` runs every frame: label text, `call_deferred(UiKit.refit)` and a layout pass. Fix: add `and not _hidden_for_pc` to the comparison.
findings.note: _process compares with 'and not _hidden_for_pc'; tutorial_test counts refreshes while seated: 20 in 20 frames before, <=1 after

findings.title: The tutorial says "the PC on the counter", but it's a desk in the back corner
findings.detail: The PC is 5 m behind the till on its own desk, and Dale says "behind the counter". New players search the counter for a PC. Fix: "Use the PC on the desk in the back-left corner, behind the till".
findings.note: tutorial step 1 and Dale's goodbye name the desk in the back-left corner behind the till (pc_desk -4.2,-7.5 vs till -3.6,-2.6); text only, check.sh clean

findings.title: The cash panel covers the tutorial's cash instructions
findings.detail: The change panel (layer 9, bottom centre, −330 to −20) covers the hint card (layer 5, bottom −36) completely during "Serve a cash customer…". At 1280 px the keypad also covers the right end of the card step's text. Fix: move the hint to the top centre (below the till hint) while the player is seated, or show the step line inside the panels.
findings.note: Seated at a till the card anchors top-centre at y 232 (under till hint + Smokes button), 520 px text with the step number inline; back to bottom on standing. tutorial_test checks card rect vs change panel, keypad and till hint (bottom card intersected the cash panel before); tutorial 42 passed

findings.title: One curious tap on the sign before any stock starts the day, and it can't be undone
findings.detail: The sign is next to the door the player walks through first. In PREP, a single E opens the store with empty shelves. The clock starts, customers come in to nothing, and there's no way back to PREP. Fix: when `world.products_in_stock()` is empty, make it a hold and say "Nothing on the shelves yet: [Hold E] open anyway".
findings.note: PREP + world.products_in_stock() empty: sign prompt 'Nothing on the shelves yet: [Hold E] open anyway' and get_hold_time 0.6; day_test taps with empty shelves and stays PREP (fails before), then stocks and taps open; day_test 48, tutorial 42 pass

findings.title: Dale's handover is easy to miss entirely
findings.detail: His lines are 2.5-second 3D bubbles with no voice. If the player heads straight for the PC (the obvious move), Dale follows at 1.25 m/s. When he reaches the seated player or gives up after 25 s, he talks behind them or from 20 m away, and the keys tween in a straight line through the shop wall. The pointer to the PC is lost. Fix: also post each Dale line as a toast, and skip the key-flight tween when there's no line of sight or the player is locked.
findings.note: Dale._say also posts 'Dale: <line>' toast; hand_over_keys frees the ring instead of tweening when the player is locked or a world ray from hand to camera is blocked. tutorial_test: player at PC gets the goodbye toast naming the PC and no flying keys (fails before); tutorial 44, menu 81 pass

findings.title: Ordering furniture on day 1 completes the tutorial's stock-order steps
findings.detail: `order_furniture` emits `Game.order_placed`, which ticks "order", and its flat-pack landing ticks "van". A player who buys a bin or shelf first skips past the Cola/Chipz/Candy/Noodles step and still has 4 free boxes unused. Fix: only notify `order_placed` when the order has stock boxes (`o.boxes.any(func(b): return not b.is_flatpack())`).
findings.note: Tutorial only notifies order_placed when the order has a non-flat-pack box; flat-packs never finish the van step. tutorial_test emits a bin-only order and checks the step stays 'order' (fails before); tutorial passes

findings.title: Market cards don't say what a product stands on
findings.detail: A card shows units per box, cost and sell price, but not the fixture kind. After a licence is bought without its fridge or freezer (K3 only fixed the licence card), the Market still sells milk or peas you can't put anywhere, and you only find out with the box in hand ("Needs a fridge"). Fix: add "Fridge · you have none" in the warning colour on the card when no placed fixture of that kind exists, reusing `AppLicences._fixture_note`'s check.
findings.note: Market cards show 'Stands on a <fixture>' and '· you have none' in WARN when no placed fixture of that kind (AppLicences.kind_placed shared with the licence note), refreshed when the app is shown. order_test: MILK with dairy licence and no fridge warns, CHIPZ doesn't (fails before: no line); order 92, m7 98 pass

findings.title: "Restock to full" orders the same boxes again while a delivery is still on its way
findings.detail: `restock_to_full` works out what is short from `World.stock_on_hand()`. That count only includes shelves, racks, loose boxes and the box in the player's hands. It leaves out boxes already paid for but not yet delivered (`DeliveryService.undelivered()`, meaning the van's cannon queue plus `pending` trips) and boxes a restocker is carrying (`StaffCrew.carried_boxes()`). A late-game cart of 60+ boxes takes several back-to-back 30-box trips. Pressing Restock to full again in that time, on the PC or the phone, puts the whole shortfall in the cart again, so the player pays twice and the bay floods. The "In boxes" line on each card also leaves out stock on the way. **Fix:** add an "on the way" count per product from `delivery.undelivered()` (count × BoxSpec units) and from `crew.carried_boxes()`. Subtract it in `restock_to_full`, and show it on each card ("On the way N").
findings.note: stock_on_hand adds on_way (DeliveryService.undelivered) and restockers' carried boxes; restock_to_full subtracts them; cards show On the way. order_test: order CHIPZ then Restock to full again -> no CHIPZ re-added (before: script error, no on_way).

findings.title: Racks can only go in the shed, which has no door into the shop, so every box goes the long way round outside and restockers can't keep up
findings.detail: `storage_rack` has `placement: "stockroom"`. The shed stands at x −22…−14, and its only opening is the roller door facing the car park (door point (−16, 0, 1.2)). After E5 the store's column 0 sits right against the shed, but `_module` just lines that wall and adds no doorway. Every rack-to-shelf trip, for the player and for restockers, goes out of the roller door, about 16 m along the apron, in through the front door, then up to 24 m into the store, and back again. [INFERENCE from coordinates] One tier-1 restocker (1.2 m/s) takes roughly 50–85 s per slot refill, about 10 refills in a 12-minute day. Four of them move about 1,000 units a day, while a level-16 store sells several thousand ((2.5+16)×0.88×1.5 ≈ 24 customers an hour × ~14-item lists). Hiring restockers barely helps. **Fix:** cut a doorway in the shared wall once column 0 row 0 or 1 is unlocked (build it in `Stockroom._module` when `store_side`, gap it in `Building`, and keep a clear strip in `BuildRules`). Or let racks stand in the shop (`placement: "any"`).
findings.note: Staff doorway shed->shop (x=-14, z -2.9..-1.5) once E5+shed; nav-only blocker + STAFF-layer NavigationLink3D so customers never route through the shed. staff_jobs_test: rack->col0 shelf staff route 12.6 m vs 38.1 m before, first item 15.8 s vs 34.8 s; restocker never leaves by roller door (before: z 1.29). build/building/nav/m5/save tests pass.

findings.title: Restockers walk a part-used box back to the rack after every slot, and never top up shelves that are half full
findings.detail: `_after_slot` always calls `_head_for_rack()` while the box still has stock, even when the next slot of the same product is 1 m away. One product usually spans several adjacent slots, so each slot costs a full round trip. `_find` also only looks at slots under `LOW_FILL` 0.5, so restockers stand idle beside racked boxes while shelves sit at 55%. **Fix:** in `_after_slot`, if `box.count > 0`, claim the nearest unclaimed slot of `box.product_id` below 100% (within ~6 m, or anywhere below LOW_FILL) and go to `TO_SLOT` before returning the box. In `_find`, when nothing is below LOW_FILL, pick the lowest slot under 100% that has a racked box.
findings.note: Part-used box chains to nearest unfull slot of its product (6 m or <50% anywhere) before returning; _find tops up slots under 100% when none <50%. staff_jobs_test: two CHIPZ slots at 10/12 -> both full with one rack return (before: never touched, 10/12).

findings.title: ShopOS apps rebuild their whole UI on every sale even when hidden, causing stutter and lost clicks
findings.file: scripts/ui/pc/app_staff.gd:35-38; app_my_store.gd:16-17; app_licences.gd:20-21; app_bank.gd:23-27; app_expansions.gd:46; app_stats.gd:35; shop_os.gd:47-74
findings.detail: Every app is built once at start and lives on hidden. On each `money_changed`/`xp_changed`/`stats_changed` (every sale, roughly every 2–3 s late game), Staff, My Store (4 categories, 19 colour buttons each with copied styleboxes), Licences, Bank and Stats free and rebuild every control, and Expansions rebuilds its cards. With the app open, a sale landing between mouse-down and mouse-up frees the pressed button, so Hire, Upgrade, Fire, Buy, Repay or Take silently does nothing on maybe ~4% of clicks. Frame cost [INFERENCE, unmeasured]: a few ms spike per sale. **Fix:** skip the rebuild while `not is_visible_in_tree()` and set a dirty flag, then refresh on `visibility_changed` (Pricing already does this). While visible, update button `disabled` and label text in place instead of freeing them.
findings.note: 4 apps gated on visibility; staff/progression/loan/menu/additions pass

findings.title: Aisle signs jump between fixtures as stock sells
findings.detail: Each category's sign hangs over whichever fixture holds the most units right now, checked every 2 s. In a large store with several gondolas of the same licence at similar fill, each sale or restock changes which one is ahead. The sign is then freed and spawned over a different aisle, so ceiling signs teleport around the store all day. **Fix:** add hysteresis, so the sign stays where it is unless another fixture beats the current one by a clear margin (e.g. 25%) for a while. Or rank fixtures by labelled capacity (sum of `slot.capacity` for slots labelled with that category) instead of live counts.
findings.note: m7 tests pass

findings.title: Restockers and customers shut cooler doors and freezer lids on each other
findings.detail: A customer's `_close_door` only checks other shoppers in PICK. If a customer opened the cooler and a restocker starts stocking it, the customer leaves and shuts the door, and the restocker carries on stocking through glass (the S14/Y8 bug again). The other way round, `_after_slot` always calls `close_door()` and shuts it on a customer who is still reaching in (the N16 bug again). On a chest freezer, a customer reaching into the other half slides the lids and closes the restocker's half. **Fix:** count who is using each fixture's door (`open_door(who)`/`close_door(who)`, close only when nobody is left), or make `_other_at` and `_after_slot` also check for staff stocking and shoppers picking at that fixture.
findings.note: Fixture.open_door/close_door take a user; door shuts when the last user is done, chest freezer keeps the needed half. staff_jobs_test: restocker finishing a cooler leaves it open for a customer still reaching in; customer leaving keeps it open for a restocker; chest lid not slid off the restocker's half. staff_jobs/progression/player/stock pass.

findings.title: A restocker still putting a box away when the next day starts is replaced by a twin, and their box is left out of the autosave
findings.detail: At PREP, `sync()` spawns a new Staff for any member whose old body `is_leaving()` and overwrites `members[id]`. The old restocker, still in WIND_DOWN carrying a box back to the shed (20–40 s at 1.2 m/s), is no longer in `members`, so `carried_boxes()` (and therefore `Save`) misses its box. End day → Pay → Next day is quick enough to trigger this, and its autosave loses up to 40 units if the player quits there. Two identical copies of the same worker (same rig seed) are also visible on the plot. **Fix:** let a leaving member go back to WORK instead of spawning a second body (reset `state` and keep the job), or have `carried_boxes()` walk the `staff` group rather than `members`.
findings.note: StaffCrew.sync calls Staff.back_to_work on a leaving member instead of spawning a second body. staff_jobs_test: restocker winding down with a box, sync -> 1 body back at work, box in carried_boxes (before: 2 bodies, box missing).

findings.title: The Market is a flat wall of 48 cards with no grouping, filter or low-stock flag, and its counts go stale while you look at it
findings.detail: The cards are in products.json order with no licence headers, search, "low/out only" filter or sorting, about 12 rows of ~250 px to scroll through. Nothing marks products that are low or empty, even though `stock_on_hand` already has `room`. "On shelves / In boxes" only updates when the window is shown, so it stays wrong while sales and van drops happen with the app open. The "Ordered N boxes, K trips" note is wiped by the next sale's `_refresh`. **Fix:** add a licence/fixture tab row and a "Needs stock" toggle that sorts by room, colour each card's stock line by how full its shelves are, refresh stock on `sale_completed`/delivery landings while visible, and keep the order note for a few seconds.
findings.note: Market: licence tabs + Needs stock (room>0, most room first), red stock line <25%, counts refresh on sale/order/box landing while open (deferred), order note held 6 s. order_test: filter/sort/tab checks, card follows shelf after a sale, note survives next sale.

findings.title: Very large orders spill past the 64-spot bay and keep dropping on the same 16 points
findings.detail: The bay plus overflow holds 2×16×2 = 64 boxes. Further trips start as soon as the van leaves. Once full, `_find` aims every extra box at `all[_next_stack % 16] + LAYER_H*2` whatever is already there, so the third layer piles up and topples into the car park. A late-game restock (several thousand units a day, ~15.5 units a box) easily goes over 64 boxes [INFERENCE: volumes]. **Fix:** hold the next trip while `bay.peek()` returns a stacking point, with a toast ("Bay full: the van waits"). Or add a third grid, or stack onto the lowest pile.
findings.note: Trip size capped by DeliveryBay.free_spots(); full bay holds the van with 'Bay full: the van waits' toast; delivery_test:test_a_full_bay_holds_the_van passes

findings.title: The cleaner goes for the nearest mess anywhere on the plot first, and waits outside in the shed
findings.detail: `_find` takes any `mess` inside `Nav.BAKE_BOX` (car park and shed included) by straight distance. Waiting in the shed, the cleaner clears empty boxes in the stockroom or car park before a spill in the shop, even though only in-shop messes cost cleanliness and satisfaction (`Hygiene.messes()` filters with `in_shop`). Each shop mess also starts with a ~16 m outdoor walk. **Fix:** rank in-shop messes (`Hygiene.in_shop`) ahead of the rest, and wait inside the shop (beside the mop bucket) rather than at `Stockroom.door_outside()`.
findings.note: CleanerJob._find ranks Hygiene.in_shop messes before others; waits beside the mop bucket. staff_jobs_test: litter 3 m away on the apron vs spill 12 m away in shop -> shop spill first (before: litter first); idle cleaner by the bucket (before: shed at -15.8,-1.0).

findings.title: A restocker can take a box from a rack you are moving in build mode
findings.detail: `_box_on_rack` checks that the box is still parented to `_rack`, but not `_usable(_rack)`. If the player picks the rack up while a restocker is in TO_RACK, the restocker walks to the old spot and reparents a box out of the floating ghost rack. **Fix:** add `and _usable(_rack)` to `_box_on_rack()`.
findings.note: _box_on_rack checks _usable(_rack). staff_jobs_test: build.carried=rack during TO_RACK -> restocker gives up, box stays racked (failed before).

findings.title: The restocker's idle status is misleading when the racks hold the wrong products
findings.detail: When the racks have boxes but none match a slot below 50%, status says "Looking for empty shelves" while the player can see empty shelves. Those products simply have no racked boxes (they are still in the bay or on the floor). **Fix:** report "Idle: no racked boxes for the low shelves (MILK, EGGS…)" by listing the low slots' products that are missing from `_racked_boxes()`.
findings.note: Idle status lists low shelves' products with no racked boxes (up to 3). staff_jobs_test: status names CANDY (before: 'Looking for empty shelves').

findings.title: Staff app "Now:" lines go blank after every rebuild
findings.detail: `refresh()` recreates the status labels empty and leaves `_status_t` alone, so they stay blank for up to 0.5 s. With a rebuild on every sale, the status lines flicker constantly late game. **Fix:** fill the label in `_member_card` straight away (`crew.members[id].status()`), or set `_status_t = 0.0` in `refresh()`.
findings.note: status filled next frame

findings.title: The queue-lane plate's BoxMesh is still rebuilt every physics frame
findings.detail: The B3 fix only caches `_plate`'s size. While carrying a till, `(_lane_plate.mesh as BoxMesh).size = …` runs every physics frame, and `PrimitiveMesh` regenerates on each set. **Fix:** set the lane plate's size once, when the carried fixture changes, like `_plate_size`.
findings.note: build tests 157/157

findings.title: Build mode re-runs every placement check every physics frame even when the ghost hasn't moved
findings.detail: `_update_ghost` calls the full `BuildRules.refusal` each frame. In a 40-fixture store that is polygon clipping against every fixture, wall, cell and access strip. It also creates and frees a `DeliveryBay` node in `bay_zones()`, recomputes `offset_polygon(poly, 0.15)` once per loose box (the whole bay), and repaints every mesh of the ghost via recursive `find_children`. [INFERENCE] Several ms a frame. **Fix:** cache on the snapped (pos, yaw) and recompute only when it changes or `fixtures_changed` fires; build the offset polygons and bay zones once per call; repaint only when the material changes.
findings.note: checks on pose change or 4 Hz

findings.title: Customers walk into fixtures placed during OPEN until you leave build mode
findings.detail: The navmesh only rebakes in `exit()`. Each `place()`/`sell()` just emits `fixtures_changed`, so walkers replan on the old mesh. They walk into the new shelf, get stuck for 3 s, then hop to the next path point through it. **Fix:** call `world.layout_changed()` after each `place()`/`sell()` during OPEN; `Nav.rebake` already merges back-to-back requests.
findings.note: BuildMode.place/sell call world.layout_changed() when StaffCrew.shift_on() (PREP-CLOSING). build_test: shelf moved during OPEN, still in build mode -> navmesh clear of its footprint (before: walkable point at its centre).

findings.title: The Furniture app orders one flat-pack per click, with a delivery fee each time
findings.detail: Kitting out a big store means dozens of clicks and dozens of $5 fees. `Game.order_furniture(id, n)` already supports a quantity with one fee, but the UI always sends 1. **Fix:** add a −/qty/+ control (Shift for 5, as in the Market) and pass `n`. Check the fixture's `max` against `owned_count + n`.
findings.note: Furniture card -/qty/+ (Shift x5), one fee, clamped to max-owned; build_test:test_furniture_app_orders_a_quantity_for_one_fee passes

findings.title: Biggest purchases are a single click with no confirmation
findings.detail: Expansions ($1,800–$4,000+, rent goes up permanently and the knock-through can't be undone), Head office ($6,000) and licences buy on one press. Selling a fixture (Del twice) and firing (Fire twice) already need a second press. **Fix:** arm the button on the first press ("Buy for $X? Press again") within 3 s, the same way as `AppStaff.fire`.
findings.note: My Store upgrades (head office $6,000) need Buy then Confirm within 3 s; progression_test:test_upgrade_buy_needs_a_confirm passes

findings.title: The Sunday paper works out the week's takings but never shows them or compares weeks
findings.detail: `write()` returns `revenue` and `customers`, but `_fill` prints neither number. There is no week-on-week line, so the weekly payoff moment says nothing about whether the store grew. **Fix:** print "Takings $X (▲/▼ Y% on last week)", using the previous 7 entries of `stats_days`.
findings.note: Paper prints 'Takings $X (▲/▼ Y% on last week)' from previous 7 stats_days; additions_test:test_sunday_paper_compares_takings_with_last_week passes

findings.title: Stars stop affecting income from about day 6, so every choice that only buys stars is dead
findings.detail: Stars only change the arrival rate (`Game.reputation` is used only in `customer_spawner.gd:50`, the HUD, the paper and head office). Arrivals soon far exceed what the 20-shopper cap lets in. At L16, 3.59 stars: 18.5×0.83×1.5×14.5 ≈ 334 arrivals a day against 127 served on day 30. Even at 1 star it would be 18.5×0.52×1.5×14.5 ≈ 209, still over the cap. Day 7 at 1 star works out to ≈85 against 63 served [INFERENCE: formula]. hours.csv shows the store at 20-26 shoppers from 09:00 to 21:00 on every day from day 14. Effect: price markups, the cleaner, bargains, the promo stand and the "found everything" bonus cost nothing and earn nothing. The profit-best markups (+25% to +79%; refusal 11-22% per item, which I computed from products.json) beat +10% by 8-56% profit per unit, and their only cost is stars that do nothing. An SS player soon learns stars are cosmetic. Fix: tie stars to basket size, e.g. a new `list.star_items` = 2 with pivot 3.5, added to `size_bonus` at `customer_spawner.gd:86` and clamped to -2..+3. Optionally scale `refuse_chance` by lerp(1.3, 0.7, (stars-1)/4). Expected: 4.5 stars ≈ +2 items per basket (≈+18% revenue, ≈+$700/day at day 30), 2.5 stars ≈ -2. Gouging then pays for itself in lost stars.
findings.note: list length x(1+0.15(stars-3.5)); test_stars_fill_baskets

findings.title: Late-game stars are capped near 4.0 because the satisfaction bonuses ignore basket size (what's left of R5 E7)
findings.detail: `queue_time` keeps counting while the till scans (`:481`), so +5 fast service needs joining the queue to paid in under 20 s. At day 30 that means 11.2 items × 1.2 s (T1 cashier) + 2.4 s card ≈ 16 s even with no queue, so the bonus is gone late. +8 found everything is all or nothing over a list of up to 20 items. Day 29 had 0 out-of-stock and 1.3% price refusals and still ended at only 3.98 stars. Days 1-5 (2-3 item baskets) sat at 4.29-4.34. Players see their rating fall as the store gets bigger and better. Fix: judge fast service on the wait before the first scan (store `queue_time` in `start_service`, `fast_service_s` 20 → 12). Give found everything when at least 90% of wanted units were bought (or scale it, +8×(1−3×misses/list)). Expected: a 0-out-of-stock day late ≈4.3 stars; typical late days 3.6 → about 4.0-4.1.
findings.note: fast service judged at first scan (12 s); found everything at >=90% units; test_big_baskets_can_still_earn_the_bonuses

findings.title: Restockers can't keep up with late-game sales, so the player spends the whole day carrying boxes
findings.detail: A restocker takes one box per trip, from racks only, and at most 4 can be hired. At day 30 the store sells 1,424 items ≈ 115 boxes/day (12.4 units per box, pop-weighted from products.json). Rack, inner door (x −14, z −2.2) and back to the shelf is about 46 m. That works out to ≈245 items per open day for a T1 restocker and ≈360 for T3, so 4×T1 ≈ 980 and 4×T3 ≈ 1,450 [INFERENCE: geometry + tier data]. Observed: ≤178 a day from staff. On days 27, 28 and 30 the AI spent 862-912 s on chores and was idle 0 s, and still lost 30-44 items to empty shelves. The player also has to carry every one of the ~115 boxes from the bay to racks that hold 64 boxes in total (8 racks × 8). SS players expect staff to take over stocking by mid-game. Fix: add `carry_boxes` [2,3,4] by tier, same product first. Raise `max` 4 → 6. From T2, idle restockers move bay boxes to free rack spots (this changes GDD §10 line 314). Expected: about 3× items per trip; 4 restockers cover ≈100% of sales by L12, and the player goes back to pricing and building.
findings.note: carry_boxes 2/3/4, max 6, T2+ haul bay->racks; tests carries_several_boxes + tier_two_racks_the_bay_boxes

findings.title: The Produce licence makes the store poorer: profit per customer pick falls 17%
findings.detail: Customer numbers are fixed by the cap (B1), so income ≈ picks × profit per pick. Produce items earn $0.54-$0.96 each, average $0.69 per pick at +10%, and carry 40 popularity weight. Buying Produce drops the store's average from $2.90 to $2.42 per pick; with every other licence owned it is $3.38 against $4.17 without Produce (−19%). Day 15, when Produce was bought, revenue per item fell from $4.04 to $3.84. Every SS player buys every licence, so this is a trap. Fix: add a per-product `pick_qty` [3,6] for produce (people buy several apples; the code already handles quantities), or raise produce market/cost about 2.5×. Expected: Produce's profit per pick ≈$2.4-$3.0, so the licence is neutral to positive.

findings.title: Expansions E1, E4 and E6 add no extra basket items, so E6 buys nothing
findings.detail: `(cells - 6) / 9` uses integer division: after E1 = 0, E3 = 1, E4 = 1, E5 = 2, E6 = 2, E7 = 3, E8 = 4. E6 ($4,000, +$30 rent/day) was bought on day 29: revenue went $7,271 → $7,206 → $7,313, i.e. flat. Fix: give each expansion its own `list_bonus` in expansions.json (e3 to e8 +1 each) and add those up in `size_bonus`. Show "+1 item per basket" on the Expansions card. Expected: each of E4 and E6 adds ≈+9% revenue (≈+$350/day at day 30).
findings.note: expansions.json list_bonus e3-e8 +1, Expansions card shows it; test_a_bigger_shop_fills_bigger_baskets

findings.title: The receipt's "Another till lets more people in" advice is false once the cap is 20
findings.detail: The hint shows whenever anyone was turned away. `min(20, 4·tills + L/2)` is already 20 at L8 with 4 tills and at L16 with 3, so tills 5-6 (or 4 at L16) let nobody extra in. Late days turn away ≈200 people (B1), so the warning shows every night and points players at $800 tills plus $90/day cashiers that add no customers. Fix: show the hint only when `max_concurrent(tills+1, level) > max_concurrent(tills, level)` and tills < 6. Otherwise say the store is at its 20-shopper limit and that faster tills and full shelves move people through quicker.
findings.note: CustomerRules.full_store_hint; till advice only when max_concurrent(t+1)>max_concurrent(t) and t<6; test_the_turned_away_advice_only_offers_a_till_that_helps

findings.title: No lunch or evening rush late: the cap flattens the time-of-day curve
findings.detail: Days 14-30 hold 20-26 shoppers from 09:00 to 21:00 even though the curve runs 0.6 to 1.6×. There are no quiet hours to restock in and no rushes to prepare for, both of which drive SS's day rhythm. Fix: scale the cap by the curve, e.g. `cap_now = max(6, round(cap × min(1, curve × 0.75)))` (morning ≈9, midday 15, rushes 20). Expected: visible rushes, quiet windows that ease B3, fewer NPCs off-peak; ≈−10-12% customers, made up by B1/B5 basket gains.
findings.note: cap_at = min(cap,max(6,round(cap*min(1,curve*0.75)))); test_the_store_fills_up_at_the_rushes

findings.title: The 40-customer star window makes the rating swing from day to day
findings.detail: Late days serve 122-134 customers, so the stars reflect the last ~3 game hours. End-of-day stars went 3.47 → 3.98 → 3.59 on days 28-30. The head-office payment (reputation at Sunday close × $1,000) is a lottery worth about ±$400 a week. Fix: window = clamp(yesterday's customers, 40, 150), or a moving average with weight 1/100. Expected: day-to-day swing ≈±0.1 and steady weekly payouts.
findings.note: reputation window = clamp(yesterday customers,40,150); test_busy_stores_average_their_stars_over_the_day

findings.title: Too much cash late with nothing to spend it on, and bills are trivial
findings.detail: Day 30: $10,094 cash, $3,883/day net; bills are $1,076, 15% of revenue. Everything left to buy (E7 $5.5k, E8 $7.5k, deli $1.5k, loyalty $3k, head office $6k, staff tiers ≈$7k, extra fixtures and tills) ≈$35k, all affordable by about day 37 [INFERENCE]. After that money has no use. Fix: with B5's basket bonus, raise E6, E7 and E8 to $6k/$9k/$14k (still paying back in ~3-4 weeks at +$350-450/day), and add one recurring sink with a real effect, e.g. a staff T4 tier or self-checkout kiosks. Expected: cash at day 30 around $2-5k and E8 still a goal.
findings.note: staff T4 tier (wages +$35/day each, $1.6k upgrades), E6/E7/E8 $6k/$9k/$14k; test_a_fourth_tier_costs_more_every_night

findings.title: The Expansion loan is never worth taking
findings.detail: $20,000 at L10 for $575/day, 41% of the day-16 profit ($1,406). The most expensive single purchase in the game is E8 at $7,500, so there is nothing to borrow it for; the AI never took it and the Business loan covers every pinch. Fix: move it to L13, make it $10,000 over 30 days, and pair it with B9's E7/E8 repricing. Expected: borrowing becomes the natural way to bring E8 forward to about day 28.

findings.title: Loyalty cards ($3,000) earn nothing
findings.detail: +3 satisfaction ≈ +0.15 stars. Stars don't move customers (B1), so the only return is head office's $1,000/star/week ≈ $150 a week, which takes 20 weeks to pay back and $0 without head office. It is the only unlock at L13. Fix: give it a basket effect (`list_bonus` +1 for members, i.e. +1 item per basket), or make it +3 satisfaction plus +1 item. Expected: about +$430/day at day 30 and roughly a 7-day payback.

findings.title: Levels 7 and 11 only unlock stockroom stages, and restockers arrive later than the stocking work

Fix: restocker L9 → L7 (paired with S2), Loyalty L13 → L11, Expansion loan L10 → L13 (B10). Expected: every level from 2 to 16 has a gameplay unlock, and help with stocking comes when the workload rises.
findings.note: restocker L7, loyalty L11 (loan L13 in B10); test_every_level_unlocks_something_to_play_with

findings.title: The first week drags: nothing new is affordable until day 6

Dairy unlocks at L2 on day 3, but licence plus multideck cost $750 against $337 cash; the AI could only buy it on day 6 with a loan. The AI was idle 172-447 s a day on days 1-5. SS players expect a first purchase within the first two days. Fix: `total_xp[1]` 500 → 350 (L2 on day 2) and dairy_multideck $500 → $300 (licence + fridge $550, affordable on day 4 without a loan). Expected: a goal and a new product line during days 2-4.

findings.title: The soak AI's habits make the late-game numbers unreliable
findings.detail: It hires exactly one restocker, racks only one spare box per product (restockers sit idle and stocked 20-178 items/day), and shelves everything itself. It never buys an upgrade (no call to `Game.buy_upgrade`; phone, loyalty and head office are untested), never upgrades staff tiers, and prices at +10%. So the "staff restock ~345 against AI 1,300" split, the stars and late cash describe the AI, not the game. Fix: hire restockers up to `max` once chores exceed 50% of open time; rack every delivered box before shelving; buy upgrades and staff tiers by payback; add a +30% pricing variant. Expected: the soak measures B1-B3 directly.

findings.title: days.csv columns shift when two loans are active, and lost_oos includes not-stocked items
findings.detail: `",".join(loans)` goes into an unquoted `%s`, so on days 15-24 ("small,business") every later column moves one place to the right: a plain CSV reader takes `restocked` as `staff_restocked`, `bills` as wrong values, and so on (I confirmed this by parsing). `lost_o` also adds `not_carried` to `out_of_stock` under the `lost_oos` header.
