findings.title: Racks get overfilled, so restockers leave boxes on the shed floor where no restocker will collect them
findings.detail: `_find_haul` adds up `StorageRack.free_spots()` (storage_rack.gd:49, just spots minus stored boxes) and claims up to `min(capacity, free)` bay boxes. It does not hold back spots for boxes already in other restockers' arms: the part-used boxes going back from a shelf trip, or another hauler's load. Two tier-2+ restockers idle in the same 0.75 s look both count the same free spots. A shelf trip takes 2-5 boxes off a rack, a hauler fills those spots straight away, and then the part-used boxes come back to a full rack. When no rack has room, `_head_for_rack` calls `_drop(box)`, which leaves a loose box on the floor beside the rack. `_find_haul` only looks inside `BuildRules.bay_zones()` and `_find` only takes racked boxes, so a box dropped in the shed stays there until the player moves it. The soak AI's "fill free rack spots" habit (B14) makes this the normal late-game state. Fix: in `_find_haul`, take away from `free` the stocked boxes in every restocker's arms and the bay boxes other restockers have claimed (`crew.carried_boxes()` plus the claims). Also let `_find_haul` pick up loose stocked boxes inside the stockroom rect, so anything already dropped gets racked again.

findings.title: The green feature wall is painted straight over the shed's staff doorway
findings.detail: `add_feature_wall` paints the whole merged run nearest the first till, corner to corner (2d943a6), with no gap for the doorway (58a68a9). With the default till at (-3.6,-2.6) from settings.json, the nearest non-front run once E5 is owned is x=-14, z 0..-12, about 10.4 m away. The back runs are at least 11.4 m away. That x=-14 run is the one `_wall_round_shed_door` splits for the doorway (z -2.9..-1.5, 2.4 m high). So on the normal progression (S1 at L2, E5 at L8, till never moved), a green plaster panel covers the opening from 1.23 m to 2.4 m while staff walk through it. Fix: when `Stockroom.has_inner_door(...)` and `_holds_shed_door(best)`, build the skin in two pieces either side of `inner_door_span()` plus a lintel piece from INNER_DOOR_H up to WALL_H, the same way `_wall_round_shed_door` does.

findings.title: Clicking a Market tab or the Needs-stock switch frees the button while it is still emitting its signal
findings.detail: `UiKit.button` connects `pressed` directly (ui_kit.gd:84). `show_tab` and `show_needs` call `_rebuild()` synchronously, and `_build_tabs()` immediately `free()`s every child of `_tabs`, including the Button or CheckButton that is emitting `pressed` or `toggled`. In Godot 4 that logs "freed … while a signal is being emitted from it", and BaseButton then keeps running on a deleted object. Tests and the soak call `show_tab()` directly, so the click path is never exercised. Other apps defer their rebuilds (my_store `_queue_refresh`). [UNVERIFIED at runtime] Fix: connect with `CONNECT_DEFERRED` or call `_rebuild.call_deferred()` from `show_tab` and `show_needs`, or `queue_free()` plus `remove_child` in `_build_tabs`.

findings.title: A missed handful of produce costs the "found everything" bonus by itself
findings.detail: B2 made the bonus allow misses up to 10% of `_wanted_units`, and `_wanted_units = p_list.size()` counts units. B4 then put 3-6 units on the list per produce pick. One refused or not-stocked produce product adds 3-6 to `_missed` (shopper_brain.gd:266/314). A 15-unit late-game basket allows 1.5, so missing one produce product loses the bonus where missing any other single product doesn't. The 15% `unstocked_pick_chance` draws from every licensed product, so a store holding the Produce licence but not stocking all six produce items triggers this often. Fix: count misses and the total per product (one per list entry or qty key), or weight each pick as one.

findings.title: A restocker opens a fresh box of a product while still carrying a part-used box of that same product
findings.detail: `_after_slot` only chains the box in hand to a slot under LOW_FILL (0.5) beyond 6 m. `_next_box` then tries the boxes in their arms with `_claim_next_slot(1.0)`. `_rack_extras` deliberately picks the same product first, so a full box of that product often qualifies for a 50-99% slot that the part-used box was just refused. The part-used box goes back on the pile and a new one is opened, so two part-used boxes of one product go back to the racks and take extra spots. Fix: in `_after_slot`, when the pile holds more of `box.product_id`, chain the box in hand with `below = 1.0`. Or have `_next_box` skip boxes of the held box's product while the held box still has stock.

findings.title: Produce handfuls give most produce shoppers a trolley
findings.detail: `uses_trolley = list.size() > basket_max_items (6)` counts units, and since B4 one produce pick adds 3-6 units. A one-pick list with 6 apples plus any second item already needs a trolley, so trolley use rises a lot after the Produce licence. Trolleys behave differently: parking, `abandon_carrier`, and the dropped "trolley" mess. Fix: compare `brain.list.size()` (distinct products) or the number of picks with `basket_max_items`, or pass the pick count separately.

findings.title: The star window is sized by sales, not visits, and shrinks after a single quiet day
findings.detail: `reputation_window()` uses `stats_days[-1].customers`, which `_count_sale` only increases for paying customers. `record_satisfaction` runs for every visitor who leaves, including walk-outs and people who give up. One poor day (empty shelves, closed early) cuts yesterday's 130-150 window to 40, and the next `record_satisfaction` pops about 100 entries at once. That brings back the day-to-day swing B8 was meant to remove; game_test `test_busy_stores_average…` even shows the collapse. Fix: count visits (a `today.visits` incremented in `_gone`, saved with the day stats) and either ease the window down by a limited amount per day or average it over a few days.

findings.title: Saved restocker boxes stack in one pile counter across all restockers, so later boxes spawn metres up
findings.detail: `pile` is set to 0 once and goes up for every box from `crew.carried_boxes()`. With 6 restockers carrying 2-5 boxes each (B3), the 12th box is saved at y = 5.55 m and the 20th at 9.55 m. They spawn above the 3.2 m ceiling and the 4.2 m shed roof, neither of which has a collider (building.gd:143-174), and drop onto the floor and shelves on load. The comment says each restocker makes its own pile. Fix: loop over `crew.workers()`, reset `pile = 0` for each worker, then add that worker's `job.carried()`.

findings.title: The level banner still plays over ShopOS while you are seated
findings.detail: `_held` is only checked in `show_level` and `set_pc_focused`. A banner that is already up when you sit down keeps showing. When it ends, `tw.chain().tween_callback(_next)` pops the next queued level without checking `_held`, so a second queued banner plays over ShopOS. Fix: start `_next()` with `if _held: _busy = false; _band.visible = false; return`, and hide or pause the current banner in `set_pc_focused(true)`.

findings.title: The aim-prompt pill stays off-centre after a window resize or UI-scale switch
findings.detail: The pill is only positioned when the prompt text changes. If the window crosses the 900 px line that `Settings._apply_ui_scale` uses (fullscreen toggle, resize), the layout goes from 1600x900 to about 1920x1080, but the pill keeps its old place until you aim at something else. Fix: reposition every frame, or on the parent's `resized` and the window's `size_changed`.

findings.title: The Options "Change helper" toggle missed the new switch style
findings.detail: V12 (01bfa7f) styled `_toggle()` (options.gd:147), the change panel and the Market, but the Change-helper CheckButton built directly at :73 never calls `UiKit.style_switch`. It still shows the default near-invisible "off" dot the commit was meant to fix. Fix: call `UiKit.style_switch(_helper)` after creating it.

findings.title: Gondola end caps hard-code the store name
findings.detail: `l.text = "CORNER TO SUPER"`, while every other name surface reads `Catalog.settings()["store_name"]` (pos.gd:67, day_summary.gd:155, shop_os.gd:108, main_menu.gd:66). Changing the name in settings.json leaves every gondola end showing the old one. Fix: use `str(Catalog.settings().get("store_name", "")).to_upper()`.

findings.title: Knock-through rubble always falls white, even when the wall coming down is the green feature wall
findings.detail: V21 says the pieces take "the wall's own finish", but the material is always the fixed plaster or wainscot colour. The start shop's feature wall is the x=-6 wall, nearest the default till, and E3 knocks it out, so the first big knock-through drops white pieces out of a green wall. Fix: if a removed piece lies on the feature-wall run (`world.building` can return that run), use `Building.STORE_GREEN` for the rows above WAINSCOT_H.

findings.title: Docs and code comments lag behind tier 4 and the box chaining order
findings.detail: GDD §10 says "2/3/4 boxes by tier" and the restocker header says "0.30/0.20/0.12 s, 1.2/1.5/1.8 m/s, 2/3/4 boxes". staff.json now has 4 tiers: 2/3/4/5 boxes, 0.08 s and 2.1 m/s at tier 4. The cleaner header still says 2.0/1.3/0.8 s, but tier 4 is 0.5. GDD also says "the next box goes to its product's emptiest slot", but `_claim_next_slot` picks the nearest slot within 6 m first. Fix: add the tier-4 numbers and say "nearest within 6 m, else the emptiest".

findings.title: The slogan test reads a private field instead of checking what's in the scene
findings.detail: `w.building.get("_slogans")` ties the test to an internal array of [segment, Label3D]. Renaming it or storing it differently fails the test (or `get` returns null) even when the lettering is fine. Fix: find the `WallSlogan` Label3D nodes under `w.building` (`find_children("WallSlogan", "Label3D")`) and check their pose against `w.building.segments`.
